text:
alex: 🚨 Seeing a sudden spike in 99th percentile latency for the serving runtime in us-west-2. P95 is stable, but tails jumped ~3x around 10:42 PT. Any known changes?

infra-bot: Deployment notice: rollout `serving-runtime@2026-03-18-10:35` completed to us-west-2 at 10:35 PT.

maria: I see the spike in Grafana, correlates with a jump in KV cache evictions and small-batch tail latency. Can someone dump a profiler sample?

jonathan: We rolled the kernel selection tweak (auto-kernel-priority) yesterday evening. It biases MatMul kernels towards the new `matmul_optim` path on H100. Not on A100.

tara: KV cache eviction rate for tenant_id=57 spiked from 2% -> 18% at the same time. Could be noisy tenant or change in batching that increases cache churn.

alex: Good call. If it's cache thrash + new kernel combo that could explain short-seq regressions. Maria, can you get a flamegraph?

maria: Uploading quick flame snapshot from 10:40-10:44 (excerpt):

```
flame_top:
  - kernel_selector::select (30%)
  - matmul_optim::dispatch (22%)
  - kv_cache::evict_loop (18%)
  - batcher::route_wait (10%)
  - io::net_recv (5%)
```

maria: Also attaching tail latency table: `p50=48ms p90=120ms p95=180ms p99=940ms` (normal p99 ~300ms).

jonathan: That `matmul_optim` path is fast for long seqs but we saw poor perf for seq<=64 in our internal bench. Might be mispredicted tiling on H100.

alex: Immediate mitigations: 1) throttle tenant 57 to reduce KV churn, 2) flip the feature flag that enabled new batching heuristic (`new_batching_v2`) back to off in prod, 3) route a portion of traffic to quantized fallback model to reduce kernel pressure. Can we do 1 & 2 now?

maria: I'm on it. Running: `./ctl feature-flag set new_batching_v2 false --env prod --force`

deploy-bot: Feature-flag change submitted: `new_batching_v2=false` by maria at 10:50 PT. Applying through rollout.

maria: Throttling tenant 57: `rctl throttle tenant=57 rate=20rps` -> done (applied to frontdoor routing).

jonathan: I'll push a temporary kernel pin for short sequences: add config `kernel_pin: matmul_generic if seq<=128`. This avoids the problematic `matmul_optim` on short path.

alex: Nice. How long for kernel pin to propagate?

jonathan: Config pushed to canaries now, deploying to 50% of capacity in us-west-2. If stable for 5m we'll flip remainder.

sre-bot: Incident runbook check: incident-serve-latency -> step 2 executed (feature flag rollback). Logging mitigation actions.

maria: After flag flip + tenant throttle + partial kernel pin: p99 dropped from 940ms -> 380ms in canary subset. Whole-region rolling apply in progress.

alex: Good. Any residual errors or QPS drop?

tara: QPS actually recovered ~5% once batching reverted. Error rate steady. KV evictions decreased to ~6%.

maria: Note: batcher logs show a sudden increase in small-batch count after the heuristic deploy yesterday — heuristic tried to coalesce very short sequences aggressively which increased interleaving across tenants and induced KV churn.

alex: Follow-ups: 1) revert the kernel selector change until we root-cause tiling decisions on H100, 2) add unit/regression test for seq<=64 on H100 perf bench, 3) adjust batching heuristic to avoid coalescing across high-variance tenants. Assign owners?

jonathan: I'll own kernel-selector revert + bench.

maria: I'll own batching heuristic tweak and regression test harness.

tara: I'll follow up on noisy-tenant detection and auto-throttle rules.

alex: Thanks team. Postmortem + timeline please. For comms: customers with impacted SLAs (list in #customer-notify) should get an update in the next 30m.

maria: Quick note — we should also add an observability metric: `kernel_path_by_seq_bucket` so we can catch path regressions sooner. Filing a ticket now.

infra-bot: Canary rollout complete at 10:59 PT. Global rollback to previous kernel selection scheduled at 11:05 PT unless issues reported.

alex: Closing loop: p99 back to ~310ms region-wide after revert. Will collect profiler data for full postmortem. Great quick coordination, :thumbsup:.

sre-bot: Incident closed (mitigated) at 11:12 PT. Please link postmortem when available.

maria: Postmortem draft started: https://docs.internal/redwood/incidents/2026-03-18-serving-latency-drift (will link once fleshed out).

jonathan: Root cause hypothesis for the record: combination of aggressive batching coalescing across tenants + kernel selection that was not tuned for short seqs on H100 -> transient KV cache eviction amplification -> tail latency spikes.

alex: Nice summary. Follow-up action items in the ticket. Thanks all.
